fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not reconstruct the central intervention: atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L followed by a 550 °C, 2 h anneal.
The proposed environmental ranges and radiation variable are not supported by the cited evidence and do not match the sulfuric-acid and cyclic molten-salt conditions of the target study.

The predicted comparison is internally confounded: specimens under aggressive conditions are expected to outperform a baseline under milder conditions, so environmental severity and passive-film state cannot be separated.
The cited findings support a Cr-rich passive-film barrier but do not establish the claimed self-healing mechanism or its behavior under irradiation.
In situ XPS of an aqueous electrochemical specimen at temperatures up to 350 °C under irradiation is not a generally feasible implementation without a specialized high-pressure operando platform.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible general passivation hypothesis, and the cited evidence reasonably supports Cr enrichment and dense oxide films as contributors to corrosion resistance. It therefore aligns with one component of the target mechanism: formation of protective Cr-containing passive products. However, it omits nearly all target-specific causal features, including the AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating, APS processing, annealing-temperature series, 550 °C optimum, grain refinement, BCC/FCC structure, Al-rich oxides, sluggish diffusion, coating defects, and molten-salt penetration. Its baseline is poorly chosen because mild exposure is not an appropriate comparator for aggressive exposure, and the study does not cleanly distinguish barrier action from self-healing. A better discriminating design would compare composition-matched coated and uncoated SS316L, as-sprayed and annealed coatings, and several annealing temperatures under identical electrolytes, while tracking film regrowth after a standardized scratch or electrochemical depassivation pulse. The evidence supports passive-film protection but not the asserted radiation boundaries or self-healing primacy.
